body_html:
Spanish false friends are words that look or sound like English words but mean something different. They are the reason a learner might announce Estoy embarazada meaning “I’m embarrassed” and accidentally tell the room they are pregnant. The good news: a small list covers most real mistakes. Here are 30 common Spanish false friends, what they really mean, and the word you actually want.

Key takeaways
  • False friends (falsos amigos) look like English but mean something else.
  • A short list of about 30 words causes most of the confusion.
  • Learn each one with the correct Spanish alternative, inside a sentence.
  • Most similar-looking words are true cognates, so don’t stop trusting them.
{{toc}}

What are false friends?

English and Spanish share thousands of related words thanks to Latin, and most of them mean the same thing. These helpful look-alikes are called cognates, and I explain them in {{link:english-spanish-cognates|English–Spanish cognates}}. False friends are the exceptions: words that share a root or a spelling but drifted apart in meaning over centuries.

Some are completely false (sopa is soup, never soap). Others are partly false: discutir can mean “to discuss”, but very often means “to argue”. Context is your best guide.

The false friends that cause the most embarrassment

Embarazada

The most famous trap. Estoy embarazada means “I’m pregnant”. To say you are embarrassed, use Me da vergüenza or Estoy avergonzado/a.

Constipado

In Spain, estoy constipado means you have a cold. If you mean the other thing, the word is estreñido, and you may want to say it quietly.

Molestar

No me molestes simply means “Don’t bother me”. It has none of the serious meaning of the English look-alike.

Excitado

A bonus false friend: excitado usually has a sexual meaning. To say you are excited about something, use Estoy emocionado/a or Tengo muchas ganas.

{{book:the-mind-lies}}

Spanish false friends in everyday situations

  • At work: Voy a asistir a la reunión means “I’m going to attend the meeting”, not help at it. Put documents in a carpeta (folder).
  • At school: a colegio is usually a primary or secondary school; university is la universidad. A lectura is a reading, not a lecture.
  • Shopping: a ganga is a bargain. Books are sold in a librería; you borrow them from a biblioteca.
  • Feelings: a persona sensible is sensitive. A sensible person is sensata.
  • Talking about time: actualmente means “nowadays”. For “actually”, say en realidad or la verdad es que.
{{image:3}}

How to remember false friends

  1. Learn them in sentences. Mi hermana está embarazada is hard to forget. Saving sentences like this is the heart of {{link:sentence-mining-spanish|sentence mining}}.
  2. Pair each with the right word. Always learn librería together with biblioteca.
  3. Make a funny mental picture. Imagine washing your hands with sopa. Silly images stick.
  4. Read a lot. Seeing words in context, especially in bilingual books, corrects false assumptions naturally. See {{link:reading-in-spanish-for-beginners|reading in Spanish for beginners}}.

When in doubt, check the dictionary

If a word feels familiar but the sentence suddenly makes no sense, you may have met a false friend. The official dictionary of the Real Academia Española lists every meaning of a word, often with regional notes, and bilingual dictionaries add example sentences that show how the word is really used. A ten-second check can save you from a very memorable misunderstanding.

Don’t let false friends scare you

It is easy to become suspicious of every similar word after reading a list like this. Please don’t. True cognates far outnumber false friends: familia, importante, información, hospital and thousands more mean exactly what you think. Trust the resemblance, and simply keep these 30 exceptions in mind.

False friends are one of the handful of tricky spots where English and Spanish part ways. To see the others, and how they fit into becoming comfortable in both languages, read my complete guide to {{link:bilingual-english-and-spanish|bilingual English and Spanish}}. You may also enjoy {{link:ser-vs-estar|ser vs estar}}, the other classic stumbling block.

Final thoughts

Every learner trips over a false friend at some point, and the story usually becomes a favorite memory. Learn the big ones, pair them with the right words, and laugh when you slip. That laugh is often the moment the word finally sticks.

faq.q: What are false friends in Spanish?
faq.a: False friends are Spanish words that look like English words but have a different meaning, such as embarazada (pregnant) or librería (bookstore).

faq.q: What is the most common Spanish false friend?
faq.a: Embarazada is the best-known one. It means pregnant, not embarrassed. To say you are embarrassed, use me da vergüenza or estoy avergonzado/a.

faq.q: Are most similar Spanish and English words false friends?
faq.a: No. Most similar words are true cognates with the same meaning. False friends are a relatively small group of exceptions worth memorizing.
